paragraphs.text: This is [first grade](anhua-dark:grades) (一级) leaf from Anhua, picked in 2015 and kept loose. In Anhua the raw leaf is sorted into numbered grades, and each grade goes into the finished tea that suits it.

Anhua County is a mountain county on the Zi river in north-central Hunan. Its [dark tea](anhua-dark:definition) is a protected origin product, so the name is tied to tea made in that place. Like every tea from the county, this one began as [heimaocha](anhua-dark:making), a raw tea of large Anhua leaf that is fixed, rolled, piled, rolled again and dried. The leaf then goes on changing slowly in warmth and moisture, which is why the trade calls [dark tea](dark:definition) post-fermented.
Eleven years have passed since this leaf was made. No set number of years makes an Anhua tea [aged](anhua-dark:ageing). It is best kept clean, dry and aired, away from mould and other smells.

brewing.text: In a small pot or gaiwan, use water at the boil and start with a steep of about 15 to 30 seconds, a little longer each round. Pressed and aged Anhua tea is also commonly simmered in a pot.

notice.text: A redder liquor, a sweeter, mellower cup, and sometimes a medicinal or herbal note.
